title: Video basics: frames, fps and temporal latents
hook: Why five seconds at 24 fps comes back as 117 frames, how a video VAE counts, and how attention cost climbs with duration.

verified.claim: Each model family's empty-latent node floors to its own grid, with the shapes in the table.
comfy/sd.py gives each VAE its ratios as functions of the latent frame count.
CreateVideo's fps sets playback and defaults to 30. LTXVConditioning's frame_rate defaults to 25.
The Wan and LTX-Video papers describe the first frame as compressed on its own.
nm_video validates and runs on a CPU.

unchecked: We did not run a VAE, so we have not confirmed each family's decoder against the ratio functions.
The attention share is a count for a plain block. It isn't a measurement of any real model.
We say nothing about which frame rate a model was trained at, or how motion quality depends on it.
